scope_note: The main islands of Mapun and Sibutu have 2,000 and 280 people respectively in 1903. January 1900 counts and dependencies are unresolved.
Act 126 continues the existing Batangas province on Luzon and the small adjoining islands. The Atlas lists Luzon and gives no detailed island inventory.

Act 116 continues Cebu and its adjacent islands and merges San Nicolas only within Cebu. Atlas lists Cebu, Camotes, Mactan and Bantayan. The 1903 island table places Mactan, Bantayan, Poro and Poson in Cebu.
Act 117 continues Bohol and its adjacent islands. 1903 groups Panglao under Bohol and Siquijor under Negros Oriental. The Atlas already lists Siquijor under Negros Oriental.
Act 121 explicitly uses the old Spanish province of Leyte and adjoining islands. The Atlas lists Leyte, Biliran and Panaon.
Act 119 explicitly adopts the former Spanish Occidental Negros. No equivalence of population enumeration definitions is established.
Act 114 continues the province called Antique on Panay. The Atlas also identifies Antique with Panay.

Both the Atlas and 1903 island table include Siquijor with Negros Oriental. Act 120 references the Spanish province on Negros itself. The mixed comparison requires both main territory and separate island population.
The Atlas lists mainland Cavite and Corregidor separately. The census includes Corregidor in Cavite. Lubang was attached in 1901 and reattached to Mindoro in 1902.
Corregidor is grouped with Cavite in 1903, where it has 707 people. It was a distinct Atlas row.
Atlas Mindoro includes Marinduque, which is a separate census area in 1903. The 1902 Mindoro law includes Lubang and adjacent islands.

The Gazetteer compiles Marinduque for six towns. Act 499 moved Marinduque and neighboring small islands to Tayabas but the 1903 census still reports the area separately. Included small islands still require comparison.
Tayabas absorbed Infanta, Principe and associated territory in 1902. Also annexed Marinduque, which remains a separate 1903 census line.
locator: Acts 417 and 499 §1 and 1903 Vol. II Table 1

scope_note: Infanta and Polillo were transferred to Tayabas in 1902.
Principe was transferred to Tayabas in 1902.
Atlas names the Manila province. In 1901, the province excluding the city formed Rizal with Morong. City limits were further specified by Act 341 in 1902.
The former province excluding the city was combined with Morong. The provincial population in the Atlas is not directly equivalent.
The Morong district became a part of Rizal in 1901.
1903 island table places Catanduanes, 39,288 people, in Albay. The Atlas publishes Catanduanes and Albay separately.
